LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down about 7% because its profit margins are running thinner than the other big defense contractors', but the underlying demand for military gear hasn't changed — so this is a margin problem to fix, not a shrinking business.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back to its deepest dip in a while, which happens periodically with this one — nothing has changed about the fact that they're the only company on earth making the machines that print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly doing its usual thing — supplying industrial gases under long contracts and nudging prices up a little at a time, with nothing dramatic happening this week.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has been the calm one lately, up while the other big tech names slid, as its cloud and AI business keeps grinding along without surprises.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is basically flat — it's the supplier of lab equipment to biotech and pharma, and demand is near the bottom of its cycle right now, with the hope being that the bioprocessing side picks back up.

CVX.sentence: Chevron eased about 4% as oil prices wobbled — remember its profits are swollen right now because Persian Gulf tensions have pushed oil far above normal, so this is the oil price moving, not anything about the company itself.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has been beaten down sharply, which looks overdone for a company whose corporate and government customers keep signing multi-year contracts for its workflow-automation and AI tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore dipped slightly even as copper prices jumped, so the miner-and-trading house is lagging a move that would normally help it — a gap that may eventually close.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta edged up, and while its reported prices look softer that's just the mix from the lime business it's buying — the actual price it gets per ton of rock is still climbing nicely.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is steady, though a weaker Mexican peso is a mild drag since most of this Latin American Coke bottler's earnings are in pesos.

UBER.sentence: Uber jumped nearly 7% and people keep booking more rides and food orders than ever — the big thing to watch is tomorrow's update and whether self-driving car companies keep choosing to run on Uber's app rather than going it alone.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading below what its own fleet of ships would cost to replace — a sign it's cheap for the long haul, even though shipping rates are quiet right now.

MA.sentence: Mastercard pushed up to new highs and is looking stretched after a strong run — but underneath, people just keep tapping their cards more than ever, which is the whole business.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot maker jumped nearly 10%, and with hospitals doing steadily more procedures on its machines — each one selling more disposable instruments — the stock is actually cheaper than its own recent norm.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia drifted down a touch as worries build about its biggest customers — Google's parent and Amazon are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — which matters because those are the people paying Nvidia's bills, not anything wrong with Nvidia's chips.
